name: Hive Backed Dollar
oneLiner: HBD is Hive's algorithmic dollar, redeemable on-chain for $1 of HIVE via a witness-set conversion, with haircut rules when system debt exceeds thresholds.
collateral: Hive protocol value and conversion rules between HBD and HIVE, including haircut logic when HBD debt exceeds protocol thresholds
pegMechanism: Protocol-level conversion mechanism targets one U.S. dollar of HIVE per HBD, with witness-set interest and haircut rules under stress

mechanismArchetypeReview.rationale: Hive's official HBD disclosure and consensus implementation establish no exogenous reserve claim: the $1 target is defended by permissionless HIVE/HBD conversions, a witness-median price feed, automatic print-stop thresholds, and a debt-limit haircut. Because stabilization and value realization depend on the protocol's native HIVE asset and consensus rules, HBD is an endogenous, reflexive algorithmic design.

oracleRisk.summary: Hive derives the HIVE/HBD conversion price from fresh scheduled-witness submissions, takes their median, and then takes the median over a 3.5-day history window; protocol-wide debt caps can constrain the effective conversion price and HBD issuance.

branchApplicability.rationale: HBD is protocol-level debt backed by the value of HIVE and converted under one consensus-wide price-feed and debt-ratio rule set. Holders do not open borrower-specific collateral positions, and Hive exposes no separately liquidatable collateral markets requiring branch rows.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Explicit Yes retained: reviewed metadata or audit notes identify direct seizure, freeze, blacklist, privileged burn, proxy-upgrade, or chain-governance intervention authority despite decentralized governance labeling.

reserves.name: Hive protocol conversion capacity
reserves.issuerOrObligor: Hive blockchain protocol (witness median price-feed conversion)

sources.label: Hive glossary (HBD conversion and haircut mechanics)

reserveReview.rationale: HBD is a native Hive protocol liability, not a claim on a segregated reserve portfolio: there are no asset reserves, only the protocol's conversion rule paying up to $1 of HIVE per HBD at the 3.5-day median witness price, bounded by debt controls. At irreversible block 108364554, total supply was 32,394,046.860 HBD and the treasury held 23,179,590.895 HBD; consensus code excludes that treasury balance, leaving 9,214,455.965 HBD in the debt calculation. Against 568,196,982.317 HIVE at 0.048 HBD per HIVE, the resulting debt ratio was 25.25345%: above the 20% print-stop threshold but below the 30% haircut threshold.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Hive protocol conversion and haircut mechanism confirmed against live chain properties
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: There is no external reserve custodian, asset allocation, or legally segregated collateral pool. HBD holders instead depend on HIVE market value and liquidity, witness price-feed integrity, the 3.5-day conversion delay, and protocol debt controls. Consensus code explicitly excludes the treasury HBD balance from the debt calculation; realized USD value after conversion remains market-dependent.

nonLinkDispositions.rationale: Backing is the Hive protocol's own conversion capacity denominated in HIVE market value — a self-referential protocol reserve rather than an exogenous asset or tracked stablecoin.

providers.name: Hive base-layer protocol (conversion mechanism; no reserve custodian)

custodyProfile.reviewer: Kimi P2 reserve cohort rc-2 (lead buidl-blackrock)
custodyProfile.uncertainty: HBD has no reserve assets to custody: backing is the protocol-native conversion rule against HIVE market value. Custody concepts (segregation, bankruptcy remoteness, rehypothecation) do not apply; the operative risks are witness price-feed integrity, the 3.5-day conversion delay, and the debt-ratio haircut degrading the $1 conversion rate when protocol debt is high.

notices.title: Protocol haircut mechanism
notices.message: HBD redemptions depend on Hive protocol conversion rules and can be haircut when system debt is above configured thresholds.

notices.title: Hive-native asset
notices.message: HBD is issued by the Hive protocol rather than an EVM-style token contract. Pharos does not list a contract address until Hive is supported in the chain metadata registry.

mintAuthority.summary: HBD is created at the Hive protocol layer through a HIVE<->HBD conversion mechanism; supply expands when HIVE is converted to HBD, bounded by a 20% print-stop threshold and a 30% hard-cap haircut. At irreversible block 108364554, consensus-counted HBD debt was 25.25345% after excluding treasury-held HBD, so hbd_print_rate was 0 while HBD-to-HIVE conversion still paid the full nominal amount.

controls.label: Hive conversion mechanism (protocol-level mint/burn)
controls.capDescription: HBD is minted via on-chain HIVE-to-HBD conversion using the 3.5-day median price. Consensus stops new HBD printing at a 20% debt ratio and haircuts HBD-to-HIVE conversion above the 30% hard limit. At block 108364554 the treasury-adjusted ratio was 25.25345%, so printing was halted but the nominal conversion payout was not haircut.
controls.evidence: Hive API state at irreversible block 108364554 reported 32,394,046.860 total HBD, 23,179,590.895 treasury HBD, 568,196,982.317 HIVE, and a 0.048 HBD/HIVE median feed. The implementation subtracts treasury HBD, producing 9,214,455.965 counted HBD and a 25.25345% debt ratio. hbd_print_rate=0 therefore reflects the 20% print stop, while the feed remained above the 30% hard-cap minimum. No permissioned minter exists: conversion is consensus-enforced and open to all users.

controls.label: Hive witness consensus set (parameter governance)
controls.evidence: Block-producing witnesses directly set the HBD interest rate. Debt-limit constants and related consensus logic change through Hive's witness-approved hard-fork process rather than a live administrator call. Witnesses govern issuance terms through consensus but do not directly mint to arbitrary accounts.

review.evidence: Hive API state at irreversible block 108364554 and the pinned consensus implementation establish the live debt controls. Total HBD was 32,394,046.860, but consensus subtracts 23,179,590.895 treasury HBD before calculating debt; counted HBD was therefore 9,214,455.965. With 568,196,982.317 HIVE and a 0.048 HBD/HIVE median feed, debt was 25.25345%. New printing was stopped, but the feed exceeded the 0.0378396893 hard-cap minimum and the current nominal HBD-to-HIVE conversion payout remained 1.0. There is no token proxy or contract administrator: HBD mint logic is base-layer consensus code changed through Hive's witness-approved hard-fork path.
